scope: SEDSnet remote-source UTC projection and absolute phase steering; no API or struct-size changes
causes: refresh_timesync_state and poll_timesync reused remote sample UTC without elapsed monotonic age
steer_unix_ms added residual correction to absolute phase error, amplifying repeated observations

red_observations.remote_projection: epoch+19 instead of epoch+20 after 20 ms

production_changes: Remote selected UTC = sample UTC + saturating elapsed monotonic milliseconds in both refresh and poll
Steering anchors to current clock and replaces pending correction with target-current; existing maximum slew/monotonic constraints unchanged
limitations: Earlier integrated finite-radio controls are not a qualification of corrected clock behavior
One-way initial time announcements still contain physical delivery uncertainty; response exchange refines the estimate
Direct no-std lib unit-test mode has unrelated std-dependent test modules; embedded production rlib and host std+embedded tests validated instead
Bare cargo check of no-std staticlib requires board-provided allocator/panic implementation; rlib compile is the SDK-only check

board_consumer_authority_correction.cause: All seven board consumer branches configured priority 0 while C API enables consumer promotion. Holdover consumers could outrank the intended RF/GroundStation authorities after source loss.
board_consumer_authority_correction.policy: Consumer fallback priority 100; RF source priority 1 and GroundStation priority 50 take over when they return. Explicitly configured board source priorities unchanged.
board_consumer_authority_correction.regression: Each board compiles actual is_source/priority helpers at consumer -1 and source 0/1/50/123. External FirmwareSimulator/tests/time-source-election uses actual SDK TimeSyncTracker to prove RF→holdover100→GS50→RF1 recovery.
board_consumer_authority_correction.status: 35 compiled board cases and actual-SDK election recovery pass; integrated matched cohort pending

board_python_suites.sanitizer_note: ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 required because execution wrapper uses ptrace, which LeakSanitizer does not support. Address/undefined behavior checks remain enabled by existing tests.
